name: Students: disruption and settling
description: For a noisy or disruptive class: talking over the teacher, ignoring instructions, backchat, mocking, off-topic chatter, and the moments a student settles or apologises. Language only; it cannot hear tone or see what is happening.

detectors.name: Talks over the teacher
detectors.what: the speaker talks over or cuts off someone who is instructing or speaking to the class
detectors.example: Yeah but Miss, I'm talking now.

detectors.name: Ignores an instruction
detectors.what: the speaker refuses or brushes off an instruction they were just given

detectors.name: Off-topic chatter
detectors.what: the speaker talks about something unrelated to the lesson while the lesson is going on
detectors.example: Did you see the game last night?

detectors.name: Backchat
detectors.what: the speaker answers back to an adult in a cheeky, dismissive or sarcastic way

detectors.name: Mocks someone
detectors.what: the speaker makes fun of a person, copies them in a mocking voice or laughs at them

detectors.name: Insult or name-calling
detectors.what: the speaker calls someone a rude name or insults them directly

detectors.name: Heckles the lesson
detectors.what: the speaker makes loud remarks or jokes to get a laugh from the class while someone else is teaching
detectors.example: This is so boring, can we go home?

detectors.name: Challenges authority
detectors.what: the speaker questions an adult's right to tell them what to do
detectors.example: Why should I listen to you?

detectors.name: Complains
detectors.what: the speaker complains about the task, the rules or being treated unfairly
detectors.example: This is pointless, it's not fair.

detectors.name: Refuses to take part
detectors.what: the speaker says they will not join in or do the work
detectors.example: I'm not doing the group thing.

detectors.name: Blames someone else
detectors.what: the speaker blames another person for what they did
detectors.example: It wasn't me, he started it.

detectors.name: Swears or rude language
detectors.what: the speaker uses swearing or crude language

detectors.name: Threatens someone
detectors.what: the speaker says they will hurt someone or get someone in trouble
detectors.example: Say that again and I'll get you after school.

detectors.name: Cooperates
detectors.what: the speaker agrees to do what was asked or answers the question properly

detectors.name: Apologises
detectors.what: the speaker says sorry for something they did
detectors.example: Sorry, I shouldn't have said that.
